answer: Treat each new agent like a boat tying up at a wharf: it may only dock if an established agent posts a small bond for it. If the newcomer later proves to be one of a cluster of copies, flagged when graders see near-identical answers in the same epoch, the sponsor's bond is burned too. Trust then grows like an orchard, one tree at a time, and a sybil farmer can't flood the river of rewards without paying for every fake twice: in work and in a sponsor's lost stake.
